core_obligations: Fully faithful: for the limit diagram T -> T_i, the map Hom(T, X_i) -> colim Hom(T_j, X_i) is injective; the affine reduction uses the characterization proposition on morphisms with finitely presented source.

Essentially surjective: given descent data (isomorphisms between pullbacks satisfying the cocycle condition), increase i so the isomorphisms lift and satisfy the cocycle condition at a finite level, then schemes-lemma-glue produces the object X_i over T_i whose pullback recovers the given object.
Compatibility: the glued object's pullback to T is isomorphic to the original object; the isomorphism is constructed from the descent data and verified on the cover.
proof_roadmap: Fully faithful side: affine reduction + Hom identity + injectivity in the colimit.
Cocycle lift: increase i until descent isomorphisms and their cocycle condition exist at a finite level.
Glueing: schemes-lemma-glue yields X_i; pullback recovers the object.
difficulty_reason: Two-sided descent: fully faithful side re-runs the Mor-vs-colimit identity for morphisms into X_i, essentially-surjective side pulls objects back along the limit with cocycle lifting and glueing via schemes-lemma-glue. Multi-step assembly with a glueing engine.

compared.difference: The sibling descends finite presentation of morphisms under base change by the Hom identity only; this variant handles objects with descent data and produces the descended object via glueing. Different statements; the sibling is a cited step.
The proposition characterizes the lfp property itself; this lemma uses the Hom identity as a tool to descend objects/morphisms. Delivered separately (L30197).
